quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure there is no oncoming traffic.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to see your blind spot when passing left.
Wait until you see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is going. Move to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces how far you can see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. Drive carefully at a reduced speed. Do not use high beam headlights. Low beam headlights work better in fog.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road unless you can clearly see ahead, you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get out and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you remain in your vehicle. Walking around outside in a snowstorm can be unsafe.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than passenger cars.
Do not need more space to turn than passenger cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Avoid staying in these areas. Trucks are bigger and heavier, so they need more space to turn and stop than passenger cars.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Traffic signal.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you about an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready for a yellow light, red light, or cross traffic.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
More accidents happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well as they do during the day. From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, or when people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, use your headlights.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead, you should:

options.text: Scan the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better when you look for and spot problems early. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look far ahead and continually scan the entire road, including the sides.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and drive with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another way across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has passed completely.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This is true even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: Crosswalks are:

options.text: Always marked with lines on the pavement.
Always marked with vertical lines on the pavement.
Always unmarked.
Either marked with lines or unmarked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either marked with lines or unmarked.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist whether they are marked or unmarked. You must stop behind a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: Driving while distracted:

options.text: Is never dangerous.
Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
Usually makes you drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows your reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: The best way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check traffic behind you several times a minute to see if another driver is tailgating, approaching too fast, or trying to pass. If a car is following too closely, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and get ready for impact.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Press hard on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need to use extra force to steer. Slow down and drive to a safe place away from traffic before stopping.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is coming up.
Trucks are on the hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or steep downhill section is ahead.

questions.question: Why should drivers watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many accidents happen because drivers did not see motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians. These road users are smaller and harder to spot than cars, even when drivers are looking. Always stay alert for them.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: You can pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You cannot pass.
You can pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed. You can only pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: You have done all you need to do.
You must wait for the police to arrive.
You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.
You can leave and do nothing else.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note that includes your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but you must first let any pedestrians or traffic still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted on the road?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and crosswalks for pedestrians.
On freeway entrance ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and crosswalks for pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at this speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign showing the maximum speed you can drive. If the road is wet, icy, or snowy, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so badly they may seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
Usually only older drivers become drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so badly they may seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look like drunk drivers. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to fight drowsiness while driving.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?

options.text: The whole rear window.
The passengers in the back seat.
Your own face in the mirror.
Most of the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The whole rear window.
questions.explanation: Adjust your rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window from where you sit. You should only need to move your eyes, not your head.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when they use sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give you directions.
They may drive one behind another.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or horns and flashing red or blue lights. Follow their loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only move forward when it is safe.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: A no passing zone is starting.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and emergency work ahead.
